claim.why_it_matters: The printed two-part listing (each part with its own underlined 'Stage' column header) became one markdown table whose header row is 'COPY statement | Text manipulation': the first column header sits outside the table as a run-on line, the second header 'Compiler directives | Stage' became a data row, and the indentation that makes 'SUPPRESS option' a sub-entry of the COPY statement is lost, so SUPPRESS reads as a peer statement. verdict.reasoning: The printed page 51 (§2002:7, page 29) shows two separate listings, each with underlined column headers ('Compiler directing statements / Stage' and 'Compiler directives / Stage'), and 'SUPPRESS option' visibly indented under 'COPY statement'. The markdown has the first header as a loose indented line outside the table, makes 'COPY statement | Text manipulation' the table header row, demotes 'Compiler directives | Stage' to a data row, and drops the SUPPRESS indentation so it reads as a peer compiler directing statement rather than an option of COPY. All entries and stage values (including the printed 'Text-manipulation' hyphen variants) are transcribed correctly. The loss of the two-part structure and of the SUPPRESS sub-entry relation is a genuine structural discrepancy, as described.
